name: DB Health
description: Provides database health information like table sizes.
project_description: DB Health monitors the size and row counts of every table in the Drupal database and records them over time so administrators can spot bloated or fast-growing tables before they cause performance problems. On each cron run (at a configurable interval) the module's size checker queries the current size and row count of every table, plus the total database size as a pseudo-table named "db", and stores each measurement with a timestamp in its own history tables. A report page at /admin/reports/db-health renders the collected history as an interactive Chart.js chart, sorting tables by size so the largest offenders are obvious. A settings form lets you pick the collection interval (from every 5 minutes up to monthly), a logs form lets you review and delete stored measurement snapshots by timestamp, and a Drush command (db-health:run, alias dh:run) forces an immediate collection. The module supports MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL, and its report, settings, and logs pages are all restricted to the 'administer site configuration' permission.
